Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: no effect
Claim: Depressive symptoms (MADRS) did not differ significantly between the vitamin D group and the control group; both groups improved over time with rehabilitation.
Sentence: "Significant intra-group difference in outcomes measures was found but not between control group and experimental group."
Measured as: Montgomery Aasberg Depression Rating Scale
Population: 40 poststroke patients (ischemic or hemorrhagic) undergoing intensive neuro-rehabilitation
Intervention: Oral cholecalciferol 2000 IU/day for 12 weeks
Comparator: No vitamin D supplementation
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 40
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: In MDD patients, depression scores (BDI) decreased after three months of vitamin D3 supplementation.
Sentence: "After supplementation with vitamin D3 for three months, MDD patients showed improvements characterized by a decrease in their BDI's scores and an increase in their serum vitamin D and ghrelin concentrations."
Measured as: BDI score
Population: Patients with major depressive disorder (40 MDD patients; 32 healthy controls for baseline comparison)
Intervention: Vitamin D3 50,000 IU weekly for 3 months
Comparator: None (before vs after in a single group)
Design: case series
Sample size: 72
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

  "rationale": "Study A is a randomized controlled trial comparing vitamin D to no supplementation (where both groups improved over time), whereas Study B is an uncontrolled before-and-after case series in patients with major depressive disorder.",
